## Research question

::: {.question}
What does it cost when a large AI data center must wait for grid energization, and how does the delay affect the developer, electricity ratepayers and society?
:::

## My contribution

First author. Developed the framework, model and analysis with Buxin She.

## Method

Present-value framework that converts delayed IT capacity into grid capacity requirements and prices the delay in separate developer, ratepayer and social ledgers, summarized by a delay cost intensity and a break-even acceleration payment; sensitivity and dependence stress tests.

## Key findings

::: {.findings}
- For a 300 MW-IT facility, a 36-month delay costs the developer on the order of $0.7 billion in present value.
- Staged energization can recover a large share of that cost.
- Ratepayer exposure depends strongly on large-load tariff design.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Boundary conditions"}
The delay is treated as exogenous and parameters are illustrative; network feasibility is not modeled, and the social perspective is illustrated with a single bridge-power example.
:::
